reading.body:
CoreWeave's public record through October 2026 shows a company filing steadily on capital and corporate events, with almost no patent footprint and no disclosed product line.

The filing cadence is the substance here. Eight SEC filings between June 10 and September 22, 2026, including a 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30 and seven 8-Ks, is a company in near-constant disclosure. That pattern fits a capital-intensive business repeatedly returning to markets or restructuring obligations, though the filings themselves are not in this data and their contents cannot be inferred from form and date alone.

The patent record is the counterweight. Two granted patents, both titled "Local Object Transport Proxy for Data Center Computing Nodes," issued March 3 and June 9, 2026, describe software for moving data between machines inside a data center. That is infrastructure plumbing, not model development. For an AI cloud, the moat is the buildings, the power contracts, and the GPUs, none of which appear in a patent count. Two patents is consistent with a company whose advantage sits in physical capacity rather than intellectual property.

What this data does not cover is decisive. There are no revenue figures, no debt or lease obligations, no megawatts, no site locations, no customer names, and no headcount. The industry classification, "Services-Prepackaged Software," is a filing-box label that sits awkwardly on a company whose business is real estate and electricity as much as code. The 321 New Jersey law exposure entries are a state-level count with no indication of what they concern. The profile text is drawn from Wikipedia and is descriptive, not financial. Anyone reading this as a picture of CoreWeave's scale or risk is reading a directory entry, not a financial statement.

profile_text.body:
CoreWeave is an AI cloud company based in Livingston, New Jersey. It rents GPU infrastructure in the cloud to AI developers and enterprises and builds its own software for managing that hardware, one of the specialist providers that grew up beside the large general-purpose clouds.

Source: Wikipedia, CoreWeave, retrieved 22 September 2026.
